issues.body: `enrolled_class_pulls` classifies candidates only by PR author, and `_mint_caller` unconditionally passes `AUTO_IMPL_ALIAS = "sol"`. But this diff changes the live impl/site/ci/default routes to `["sol", "opus5"]`, explicitly allowing Opus to author when Sol is unavailable. Such an Opus-authored PR is therefore minted as OpenAI/Sol; `REVIEW_CHAIN` then selects Opus as reviewer, so an Anthropic-authored change can receive an Anthropic review while the record falsely satisfies the cross-provider check. The same problem applies to historical Anthropic-authored PRs missing records: there is no creation-time or actual-dispatch evidence check before the constant is recorded. The new self-tests merely assert that the pinned alias resolves to OpenAI and cannot detect this false attestation.
issues.fix_hint: Bind `impl_provider`/`impl_alias` to trustworthy per-PR dispatch or authorship evidence and refuse when it is absent or inconsistent. At minimum, do not auto-mint a Sol record for PRs that may have been produced by the Opus fallback or by the prior Anthropic-first protocol; add an end-to-end test where an Opus fallback authored the PR and prove the lane either records Anthropic and selects OpenAI review or fails closed.
issues.title: The sweep fabricates OpenAI provenance for permitted Anthropic fallback implementations

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The provider inversion is not sound for the implementation routes introduced here. The unattended writer now asserts that every enrolled-author PR was implemented by Sol/OpenAI, while the same diff explicitly permits Opus/Anthropic to implement when Sol is unavailable. That can turn same-provider Opus review into an apparently cross-provider approval. The tests pin the new literals but do not exercise the contradictory fallback-authorship case.
